text: Welcome back to my channel! Today I'm taking you on my incredible seven-day journey through Japan.
We'll be starting in Tokyo, the world's most populated metropolitan city.
My first stop was the legendary Shibuya Crossing — and honestly nothing prepares you for it.
Over 3,000 people cross at a time. It's the busiest pedestrian intersection on the planet.
Day two I headed to Asakusa to visit Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple.
The Nakamise shopping street leading up to the temple is absolutely packed with tourists and locals alike.
In the afternoon I visited teamLab Planets in Toyosu — a digital art museum unlike anything I've ever seen.
You literally walk through water as part of the installation. Book tickets months in advance.
Day five in Kyoto was my favourite. I woke up at 4am to hike Fushimi Inari before the crowds arrived.
Ten thousand torii gates stretch up the mountain behind Fushimi Inari Taisha shrine.
After Fushimi Inari I took a bus to Arashiyama to walk through the famous bamboo grove.
The bamboo grove at Arashiyama is surreal — especially early in the morning when it's quiet.
I also visited the Tenryu-ji temple gardens right next to Arashiyama — incredible views of the mountains.
Day six I visited Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion. It's genuinely gold-leafed and reflects perfectly in the pond.
Then I browsed Nishiki Market — Kyoto's kitchen — for pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, and matcha everything.
Day seven: Osaka. I spent the whole day at Dotonbori eating my way through takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and ramen.
The Glico Running Man sign at Dotonbori is the most photographed spot in Osaka — it's iconic.
I also hit Kuromon Ichiba Market for fresh uni, wagyu skewers, and the most amazing crab I've ever eaten.
If I had to pick one food from this entire trip it would be the gyoza from this tiny restaurant near Shinsaibashi.
Japan completely exceeded my expectations. The temples, the food, the people — all absolutely incredible.
Drop any Japan questions in the comments and I'll see you in the next one!
